## Addendum — 2026-09-15T07:58Z: two more channels measured, and they normalize differently

Taken while running the decision-box backfill on this lane (six `PATCH /issues/{n}` writes and one `POST /issues/{n}/comments`), so these are incidental readings from real writes, ⛔ not a synthetic probe.

### ① `PATCH /issues/{n}` — issue BODY — append-if-missing, no normalization

Six writes, each with a **pre-registered prediction** of the stored byte count before the request went out:

| card | sent body ends with a footer? | sent bytes | predicted stored | actual stored | stored == sent + footer, byte for byte? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| #7911 | no (card had none) | 5306 | 5364 | **5364** | **yes** |
| #8572 | no (its own footer stripped first) | 6538 | 6596 | **6596** | **yes** |
| #8603 | no (card had none) | 12324 | 12382 | **12382** | **yes** |
| #8800 | no (card had none) | 9316 | 9374 | **9374** | **yes** |
| #8961 | no (its own footer stripped first) | 9041 | 9099 | **9099** | **yes** |
| #9263 | no (its own footer stripped first) | 12375 | 12433 | **12433** | **yes** |

⇒ **+58 bytes every time, and the result is the sent text with the footer concatenated verbatim** — no separator rewriting, no trailing-whitespace change. 6/6.

⛔ **What these six do NOT establish.** Every one of them was sent *without* a trailing footer (deliberately: stripping first makes the prediction hold under both the `无条件` hypothesis and the append-if-missing one, so the writes stayed safe while the question was open). So they measure the append, ⛔ not the conditionality, on this endpoint. The conditionality reading in the card's original body stands on the comment-endpoint writes, not on these.

### ② `POST /issues/{n}/comments` — a body that ALREADY ends with a footer is NORMALIZED, not duplicated

Comment `5676785328` on objectui#5734. Sent 4117 bytes ending with a footer; stored **4117 bytes** — so `+0`, consistent with the card's headline.

⚠️ But ⛔ `+0` is not identity, and here it is not: equal byte counts, **53 differing character positions**. Located by first-differing-index, ⛔ not by byte count:

- sent tail: `gap.**` `\n` `\n` `---` `\n` `_Generated …_` `\n`
- stored tail: `gap.**` `\n` `\n` `\n` `---` `\n` `_Generated …_`

⇒ the trailing newline is stripped (−1) and a newline is **inserted before the `---` rule** (+1), so the footer ends up separated by a blank line. Net zero, which is exactly why a byte-count check reads it as "unchanged" and a naive equality check reads it as "clobbered". Neither is true: the channel **normalizes the footer's separator**.

### Why this matters for the clause as written

AGENTS.md clause ③ says the append is `无条件` and that the stored body is **exactly 58 bytes** longer. Across these two endpoints:

- the `+58` half holds on the issue-body endpoint when no footer is present (6/6, byte-exact);
- the `无条件` half is still falsified by the comment-endpoint writes in this card's original measurement;
- and a third behaviour the clause does not mention at all now has a reading: the **comment** endpoint rewrites the separator around an existing footer, while the **issue-body** endpoint concatenates without touching anything. A seat that verifies a write by byte count will miss it; a seat that verifies by equality will misread it as a failed write. The repair for both is the same instrument this seat now uses by default: **predict the stored bytes before the request, then compare by first differing index.**

⛔ Not measured, and not to be assumed from the above: whether `PATCH /issues/{n}` with a body that already ends with a footer duplicates it or normalizes it. That is the one cell of the matrix still empty, and filling it means deliberately sending a footer-terminated body to a real card.
